account:
Today's unusual business appears to be rumours growing out of ordinary delivery questions. At tea, the neighbour said they personally heard Freight offer wheat collection and bread delivery to the baker. The neighbour heard talk of bridge or port changes and decorations, with Townsfolk 02 named as a source, but obtained no firsthand details. The baker reportedly knew of no celebration. I have neither witnessed such changes nor authorized them, so I cannot treat these stories as announcements. Freight's activity may simply be intended to arrange grain collection and bread distribution; I do not know of any larger purpose.

The builder reported no confirmed damage at the bridge, ferry, or warehouse. I requested specific locations and itemized estimates rather than approving speculative work. No paid inspection or repairs were authorized, and the builder acknowledged that decision. During town accounts I personally checked the treasury: 128 emeralds, none removed. There was no ledger there, leaving income and expenditure unverified. The secretary says the balance and no-spending decision have been recorded in the office chest.

My appointments have occupied the day: market, lunch, accounts, and tea at the east-bank cottage. The neighbour confirmed tomorrow's tea at the same cottage at three. I returned to the office for the afternoon appointment, arriving at 16:50. There are now two written books in the chest; I have not read their contents. I have just asked the secretary about correspondence, meeting requests, and the new record, and am awaiting a reply. Nothing I have learned establishes a secret project, celebration, or actual infrastructure alteration.
